_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: Houston ISD's Future 2 model puts AI literacy beside screen-free experiences. The school schedule and the district's unfinished AI policy answer different questions.

introduction.text: Houston ISD is reorganizing the school day around a distinction between academic foundations and hands-on learning. Its [Future 2 model](c7) keeps the district's standard curriculum in the morning and places experiences and workshops in the afternoon.

AI appears in that model in different ways. The schedule names coursework in AI literacy and design thinking. An optional AI-driven reading and math platform is available to students who meet the district's testing criteria.

paragraphs.text: The district describes its afternoon experiences as [screen-free](c6). That statement applies to those experiences, not every activity in the school day. It can coexist with the separately described AI coursework and accelerated learning platform.

The campus page lists schools in pairings. The launch announcement described an initial conversion, while later reporting described a wider rollout. Those documents should not be treated as identical snapshots of the program.

sections.heading: The policy was still a separate matter

paragraphs.text: Houston ISD's [board policy on artificial intelligence](c16) reached a second reading in August. The record checked for this edition did not establish passage. A published school model is not proof that the board adopted the policy governing AI use.

Katy ISD's separate framework explicitly places responsibility for lessons and evaluation with educators. Temple ISD described a phased student rollout after staff training. Neither district's approach establishes Houston's rules.

The schedule explains the proposed learning model. A final board action would settle the status of the AI policy. Until that action is verified, the program description and the policy's approval status need to remain separate.
